title: Code and Expression Injection via eval/exec
platform_conditions: CPython 3.x standard library; applies on every OS and deployment target
security_mechanism: eval/exec compile the attacker-influenced string to Python bytecode and run it with the caller's namespaces; the string is code, so any statement-level capability (imports, attribute traversal, attribute assignment) is available. Passing {'__builtins__': {}} does not sandbox it: literals can reach object dunder chains (().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()) to recover dangerous types. The same class of flaw appears via str.format when the format string itself is attacker-controlled ('{0.__class__}' traverses attributes) and via templates constructed from input.

source_sink_clues.source: User-supplied expression strings: query parameters, JSON fields reused as formulas or rules, calculator/policy expressions, attacker-controlled format strings or template text.
source_sink_clues.sink: eval() / exec() / compile() on dynamic strings; __import__ and importlib.import_module with dynamic names; str.format called with an attacker-controlled format string

tracking_guards: Verify the expression is parsed by ast.literal_eval (literals only, no name resolution) or matched against a strict grammar/allowlist of identifiers and operators before evaluation; verify format strings are compile-time constants with only the values dynamic; treat any eval/exec reachable from input as a candidate unless such a structural guard is present.
not_candidate_when: The evaluated string is a compile-time constant, the input is strictly validated to a numeric/whitelisted grammar before reaching eval, ast.literal_eval is used instead of eval, or the format string is a constant and only substitution values are dynamic.
public_references: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html
